exam.subject: General Knowledge
exam.school: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examination (ESSCE) – national
exam.title: Eritrean Secondary Education Certificate Examinations 2020 – General Knowledge (0134)

parts.title: Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: This examination paper contains 100 multiple choice questions only. You must answer all of them. Each question carries one point. There is only one best answer for each question; blacken the letter of your choice on the SCANTRON answer sheet with a pencil.

source.prepared_by: Ministry of Education, Eritrea – ESSCE 2020, General Knowledge, exam code 0134
source.conversion_notes: CamScanner scan. Text from tesseract OCR, corrected against the 150-dpi page images (the OCR of pages 13–21 was badly garbled and those items were re-keyed from the images). Underlining in the paper (‘not’/‘is not’ in items 1, 10, 15, 17, 18, 19, 23, 41, 49, 57, 77, 88, 95; ‘different’ in 21, 47, 54, 68; ‘dissimilar’ in 62; ‘is true’ in 39; ‘except’ in 27 and 97) is marked <u>…</u>. Blanks printed in items 11 and 46 are shown as ______. Printed typos are kept where harmless (e.g. ‘Pierre-Emerick Aubamey’, ‘Robel Teklemichel’). No figures.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key exists. All answers were solved independently and every fact was checked against reliable general sources (official Eritrean sources such as shabait.com for local facts; encyclopaedias, UN/agency sites and news archives for world facts). General Knowledge has no textbook: textbook_ref = {source:'general', reference, time_sensitive}. Current-affairs items are answered as correct at the time of the exam (the 2020 ESSCE was sat from 18 March 2020, per shabait.com – so events up to early 2020, such as the December 2019 CECAFA Cup and Ethiopia's December 2019 satellite launch, are current); later changes are noted in the explanation.
exam.textbook_note: No General Knowledge textbook: every textbook_ref is a general-source reference {source:'general', reference, topic, accessed, time_sensitive}.

questions.stem: One of the following statements <u>is not</u> true about deserts.

options.A: People and animals do live in deserts.
options.B: Sahara is the largest desert in the world.
options.C: Deserts are created by masses of dry air.

explanation_steps: A desert is defined by dryness (very low precipitation, under about 250 mm a year), not by heat – so ‘all deserts are dry’ is true.
Many deserts are cold: Antarctica, the Arctic, the Gobi. So ‘All deserts are hot’ is false. Answer: E.
Note: strictly, the largest desert is Antarctica (a cold desert); the Sahara is the largest HOT desert, so B is also inaccurate.
tips: Desert = dry, not necessarily hot.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a cold desert?
explanation_steps: The Gobi in Mongolia/China has very cold winters. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Desert; National Geographic – deserts

questions.review_flag: Two false statements: E (all deserts are hot) is intended, but B is also strictly false (Antarctica is the largest desert; the Sahara is the largest hot desert). Both accepted.

questions.stem: The three countries that formed the Axis during World War II were?
explanation_steps: The Axis powers were Germany, Italy and Japan (Tripartite Pact, 1940).
Britain, France, the USA and the Soviet Union (Russia) were the Allies. Answer: C.
tips: Axis = Rome–Berlin–Tokyo.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these countries was one of the Allied Powers in World War II?
explanation_steps: The Soviet Union fought with the Allies. Answer: D.

questions.stem: One of the following planets has more similarities with the Earth.
explanation_steps: Venus is called Earth's ‘twin’ or ‘sister planet’: it is nearest to Earth and has almost the same size, mass, density and gravity.
Mars resembles Earth in day length, seasons and rocky surface, but is only about half Earth's diameter. Mercury is tiny; Jupiter and Uranus are giant gas/ice planets.
The usual textbook answer is Venus (B); Mars (C) is also defensible.
tips: Venus – Earth's twin in size; Mars – most Earth-like in conditions (day, seasons).

similar_questions.stem: Which planet is known as the ‘Red Planet’?
explanation_steps: Iron oxide on its surface makes Mars look red. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: NASA Solar System Exploration – Venus; Mars

questions.review_flag: Ambiguous: Venus (similar size/mass) and Mars (similar day, seasons, surface) are both ‘similar to Earth’. Keyed B; C also accepted.

questions.stem: One of the following will likely happen in the absence of the Earth’s gravity.

options.A: Things will get stuck to the surface of the Earth.
options.B: People would start standing on their heads.
options.C: The moon would continue to go around the Earth.
options.D: Air pressure on the surface of the Earth would increase.
options.E: Things would fly off to space.

explanation_steps: Gravity holds objects, air and the Moon to the Earth. Without it, loose objects (and the atmosphere) spinning with the rotating Earth would move off in straight lines into space.
The Moon would stop orbiting and air pressure would fall, not rise. Answer: E.
tips: Gravity = the force that keeps things on Earth and keeps the Moon in orbit.

similar_questions.stem: What keeps the Moon in orbit around the Earth?
explanation_steps: The Earth's gravitational pull provides the centripetal force for the Moon's orbit. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Automation refers to operations by machines that are

options.C: programmed to run nearly independent of human control.

explanation_steps: Automation is the use of machines and control systems (computers, robots, sensors) that run a process with little or no human intervention.
Answer: C.
tips: Automation reduces the need for labour – the opposite of ‘large work force’.

similar_questions.stem: A machine that carries out tasks automatically, often in factories, is a
explanation_steps: Industrial robots perform automated tasks. Answer: A.

questions.stem: The set of instructions that a computer uses to manipulate data is called a
explanation_steps: Software = programs, i.e. sets of instructions that tell the computer what to do with data.
Hardware (CPU, microprocessor, network devices) is the physical equipment. Answer: A.
tips: Software = instructions you cannot touch; hardware = parts you can touch.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of software?
explanation_steps: Microsoft Word is an application program (software). Answer: C.

questions.stem: What is the next number in the series, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64?
explanation_steps: Each term is double the previous one (powers of 2).
tips: Check ratios as well as differences in a number series.

similar_questions.stem: What is the next number: 3, 9, 27, 81, …?
explanation_steps: Each term × 3: 81 × 3 = 243. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Queen Nefertiti was a ruler of ancient
explanation_steps: Nefertiti (14th century BC) was the queen and co-ruler of Pharaoh Akhenaten of Egypt; her painted bust is famous.
Answer: C.
tips: Famous Egyptian queens: Hatshepsut, Nefertiti, Cleopatra.

similar_questions.stem: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of
explanation_steps: Cleopatra was the last ruler of the Ptolemaic kingdom of Egypt (died 30 BC). Answer: B.

questions.stem: The first European, who sailed from Europe through South Africa to India, was
explanation_steps: The Portuguese Vasco da Gama sailed around the Cape of Good Hope and reached Calicut, India, in May 1498.
Magellan's expedition first circumnavigated the globe; Cook explored the Pacific; Marco Polo went overland to China; Mungo Park explored the Niger. Answer: A.
tips: Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape (1488); da Gama went on to India (1498).

similar_questions.stem: Who was the first European to sail around the southern tip of Africa (1488)?
explanation_steps: Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following African countries is <u>not</u> a landlocked country?
explanation_steps: Cameroon has a coastline on the Gulf of Guinea (Atlantic Ocean), with the port of Douala.
South Sudan, Niger, Mali and Zambia have no coast. Answer: D.
tips: Africa has 16 landlocked countries, including Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, Rwanda, Mali, Niger, Chad, Zambia.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these countries is landlocked?
explanation_steps: Ethiopia has had no coast since Eritrea's independence. Answer: B.

questions.stem: ______ dogs do not bite.
explanation_steps: The proverb is ‘Barking dogs seldom (do not) bite’: people who make loud threats rarely act on them.
Answer: C.
tips: Complete well-known proverbs by memory; then think of the meaning.

similar_questions.stem: ‘Empty vessels make the most noise’ means

options.B: people with little knowledge often talk the most

explanation_steps: Foolish or ignorant people tend to talk the most. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Oxford Dictionary of Proverbs – ‘barking dogs seldom bite’

questions.stem: In 1955, one of the following persons became the Chief Executive of the Eritrean Government.
explanation_steps: Tedla Bairu was the first Chief Executive (1952–1955) of federal Eritrea; he resigned in July 1955 under Ethiopian pressure.
Asfaha Woldemikael, a unionist, was elected Chief Executive in 1955 and served until the federation was dissolved in 1962. Answer: D.
tips: Federation (1952–1962): Chief Executives Tedla Bairu (1952–55) and Asfaha Woldemikael (1955–62); Idris Mohammed Adem was President of the Assembly.

similar_questions.stem: Who was the first Chief Executive of the Eritrean government under the federation (1952)?
explanation_steps: Tedla Bairu became Chief Executive in 1952. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eritrea (federation period); Tekeste Negash, Eritrea and Ethiopia: the Federal Experience (1997)

questions.stem: John Ruskin, a British writer once said, “All books are divisible into two classes, the book of the hour and the book of all time.” What does this statement mean?

options.A: All books remain popular for all times.
options.B: All books become unimportant after a short period of time.
options.C: All books are good only for a while.
options.D: Some books remain popular and important for a long period of time.
options.E: Some books are useless at any time.

explanation_steps: Ruskin contrasts books that are useful only for a short time (‘of the hour’) with books that stay valuable for ever (‘of all time’).
So some books remain popular and important for a long time. Answer: D.
tips: Quotation items: restate each half in your own words, then choose the option that keeps both halves.

similar_questions.stem: ‘Knowledge is power’ (Francis Bacon) means

options.A: knowledge gives the ability to act and influence

explanation_steps: Knowledge gives people the ability to do things and to influence events. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: John Ruskin, Sesame and Lilies (1865), lecture ‘Of Kings' Treasuries’

questions.stem: Which of the following words is spelt correctly?
explanation_steps: The correct spelling is ‘aggressive’ – double g and double s.
Answer: C.
tips: Aggressive: ‘gg’ and ‘ss’ (like aggression).

similar_questions.stem: Which word is spelt correctly?
explanation_steps: ‘Accommodate’ has double c and double m. Answer: C.

questions.stem: One of the following Eritrean languages does <u>not</u> belong to the Semitic linguistic group.
explanation_steps: Tigrigna, Tigre and Arabic are Semitic languages.
Bilen is a Cushitic (Agaw) language. Answer: D.
tips: Eritrean language families: Semitic – Tigrigna, Tigre, Arabic (Rashaida); Cushitic – Bilen, Afar, Saho, Hidareb (Beja); Nilo-Saharan – Kunama, Nara.

similar_questions.stem: Which Eritrean language belongs to the Nilo-Saharan family?
explanation_steps: Kunama (like Nara) is Nilo-Saharan. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – Eritrea's nine ethnic groups; Ethnologue – Bilen (Central Cushitic)

questions.stem: A person is said to be unemployed if she/he

options.B: is not looking for a job.
options.C: is sick and unable to work.
options.E: is looking for a job, but has not found one.

explanation_steps: An unemployed person is someone of working age who is able and willing to work, is actively looking for work, but has no job (ILO definition).
Retired, sick or voluntarily idle people are outside the labour force. Answer: E.
tips: Unemployed = able + willing + actively seeking + no job.

similar_questions.stem: A trained teacher who works only 10 hours a week because no full-time job is available is
explanation_steps: Working less than he wants/can = underemployment. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: International Labour Organization – definition of unemployment

questions.stem: One of the following countries has <u>not</u> landed a space craft safely on the moon yet.
explanation_steps: Soft landings on the Moon by the exam date (March 2020): Soviet Union/Russia (Luna 9, 1966), USA (Surveyor 1, 1966; Apollo), China (Chang'e 3, 2013; Chang'e 4, 2019).
India's Chandrayaan-2 lander Vikram crashed in September 2019, so India had not yet landed safely. Answer: D.
tips: Time-sensitive: India achieved a soft landing with Chandrayaan-3 on 23 August 2023.

similar_questions.stem: In 2019 China's Chang'e 4 became the first spacecraft to land on

options.B: the far side of the Moon

explanation_steps: Chang'e 4 landed on the far side of the Moon on 3 January 2019. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: NASA / ISRO – Chandrayaan-2 (2019) and Chandrayaan-3 (2023) missions
textbook_ref.note: Correct at the exam (2020); India landed Chandrayaan-3 near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, so today no option would be correct (Japan also landed in 2024).

questions.stem: Which of the following political parties did <u>not</u> exist in the late 1940’s in Eritrea?
explanation_steps: The parties of the late 1940s (British Administration period) were the Unionist Party, the Muslim League (1946), the Liberal Progressive Party (1947) and the Pro-Italy Party.
The Eritrean Liberation Movement (Haraka, Mahber Shewate) was founded in 1958, in Port Sudan. Answer: C.
tips: 1940s = political parties under the BMA; 1958 = ELM; 1961 = ELF armed struggle; 1970s = EPLF.

similar_questions.stem: The Eritrean armed struggle for independence began on 1 September 1961 under the leadership of
explanation_steps: Hamid Idris Awate fired the first shots at Mount Adal. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – history of the Eritrean struggle; Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eritrea (British administration)

questions.stem: A person who does <u>not</u> believe in any god is called a/an
explanation_steps: An atheist does not believe in any god (a- = without, theos = god).
Monotheist – one god; polytheist – many gods; animist – spirits in nature; dualist – two opposing principles. Answer: D.
tips: mono = one, poly = many, a- = without.

similar_questions.stem: A person who believes in only one God is a
explanation_steps: mono (one) + theist → monotheist. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Oxford Learner's Dictionary – atheist, monotheist, polytheist

questions.stem: Kilobyte, Megabyte, and Gigabyte refer to

options.A: devices that input data to a computer.
options.B: devices that print documents from a computer.
options.C: the central processing unit in a computer.
options.D: the memory capacity of a computer.

explanation_steps: Bytes and their multiples measure amounts of data – memory and storage capacity.
1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB. Answer: D.
tips: Bit < byte < kilobyte < megabyte < gigabyte < terabyte.

similar_questions.stem: Which is the largest unit?
explanation_steps: 1 TB = 1024 GB. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following words is <u>different</u> from the others?
explanation_steps: Watch, match, catch and fetch all end in ‘-tch’.
‘Wash’ ends in ‘-sh’. Answer: C.
tips: In word odd-one-out items look at spelling patterns as well as meaning.

similar_questions.stem: Which word is different from the others?
explanation_steps: Light, night, might and fight end in ‘-ight’; lift does not. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Who is the first woman to fly in space?
explanation_steps: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova orbited the Earth in Vostok 6 on 16 June 1963.
Sally Ride (1983) was the first American woman; Kalpana Chawla the first Indian-born woman. Answer: B.
tips: Firsts in space: Gagarin (first man, 1961), Tereshkova (first woman, 1963).

similar_questions.stem: Who was the first American woman in space?
explanation_steps: Sally Ride flew on the Space Shuttle in 1983. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> part of the Red Sea?
explanation_steps: The Gulfs of Suez and Aqaba are the two northern arms of the Red Sea, and the Gulf of Zula (Annesley Bay) is an inlet on the Eritrean coast.
The Gulf of Aden lies beyond the Bab-el-Mandeb strait and belongs to the Arabian Sea/Indian Ocean. Answer: D.
tips: Red Sea ends at Bab-el-Mandeb; then comes the Gulf of Aden.

similar_questions.stem: The Gulf of Zula (Annesley Bay) lies south of which Eritrean port?
explanation_steps: The Gulf of Zula is just south of Massawa. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Red Sea; Gulf of Aden

questions.stem: An instrument that is used to measure the speed of wind is a(an)
explanation_steps: An anemometer (cup anemometer) measures wind speed.
A barometer measures air pressure; a wind vane shows wind direction; a clinometer measures slope angles. Answer: B.
tips: Weather instruments: thermometer – temperature; rain gauge – rainfall; hygrometer – humidity.

similar_questions.stem: Which instrument shows the direction of the wind?
explanation_steps: A wind vane points into the wind. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Meteorological Organization – Guide to instruments

questions.stem: If the average level of price increases, the situation is called
explanation_steps: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general (average) price level.
Deflation is a fall in the price level; recession/depression are falls in output. Answer: B.
tips: Inflation reduces the purchasing power of money.

similar_questions.stem: A continuous fall in the general price level is called
explanation_steps: Deflation. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Business and Economics Grade 12 (inflation); IMF – ‘What is inflation?’

questions.stem: What type of medicine do diabetic patients take?
explanation_steps: Diabetes mellitus is a lack of (or resistance to) insulin, the pancreatic hormone that lowers blood glucose; many patients inject insulin.
Penicillin is an antibiotic and Panadol a painkiller; glucose would raise blood sugar further. Answer: D.
tips: Insulin – from the pancreas – lowers blood sugar.

similar_questions.stem: Insulin is produced by the
explanation_steps: The beta cells of the pancreas produce insulin. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization – Diabetes fact sheet

questions.stem: The use of the following fuels contributes to global warming, <u>except</u>
explanation_steps: All five fuels release carbon dioxide when burned, so strictly each contributes to global warming.
Natural gas is usually taught as the ‘cleanest’ fuel (least CO₂ and soot per unit of energy), so it is the most likely intended answer.
Wood could also be argued (carbon-neutral if the trees are replanted), but cutting trees for firewood and charcoal is a major cause of deforestation in Eritrea. Answer: E (intended).
tips: Coal emits the most CO₂ per unit of energy, natural gas the least of the fossil fuels.

similar_questions.stem: Which fossil fuel produces the least carbon dioxide per unit of energy?
explanation_steps: Natural gas (methane) emits about half the CO₂ of coal per unit of energy. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: US EIA – carbon dioxide emissions coefficients by fuel; IPCC AR5

questions.review_flag: Defective: every listed fuel emits CO₂ when burned, so no option is strictly correct. Keyed E (natural gas, ‘clean’ fuel); A (wood, renewable) could be argued.

questions.stem: We cannot satisfy all of our needs because
explanation_steps: The basic economic problem (scarcity): human wants are unlimited while the resources to satisfy them are limited.
Both A and B together explain it. Answer: E.
tips: Scarcity = unlimited wants + limited resources → choice and opportunity cost.

similar_questions.stem: The value of the next best alternative given up when making a choice is called
explanation_steps: That is the opportunity cost. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Business and Economics Grade 10 (scarcity and choice)

questions.review_flag: C (‘needs are not satiable’) means the same as A; keyed E (A and B) as the complete answer.

questions.stem: Akberet is a woman of substance. According to this statement, Akberet is
explanation_steps: ‘A woman/man of substance’ is a person of importance, strength of character and ability (sometimes also wealth).
Answer: C.
tips: ‘Of substance’ = important, solid, capable – not about appearance.

similar_questions.stem: ‘He is a man of his word’ means he
explanation_steps: A man of his word keeps his promises. Answer: B.

questions.stem: In the 2019 CECAFA football match in Uganda, the finalist teams were
explanation_steps: In the final of the 2019 CECAFA Senior Challenge Cup (Kampala, 19 December 2019) Uganda beat Eritrea 3–0.
It was Eritrea's first appearance in a CECAFA senior final. Answer: A.
tips: Follow the Red Sea Camels' results in regional competitions.

similar_questions.stem: Which country won the 2019 CECAFA Senior Challenge Cup?
explanation_steps: Uganda won its record 15th title. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Kawowo Sports, ‘Uganda Cranes lift the 2019 CECAFA Senior Challenge Cup’, 19 Dec 2019; ENFF

questions.stem: The abbreviation, AI, stands for
explanation_steps: AI = Artificial Intelligence: computer systems that perform tasks normally needing human intelligence (recognising speech, translating, learning).
Answer: B.
tips: Common abbreviations: AI, ICT, GPS, USB, WWW.

similar_questions.stem: GPS stands for
explanation_steps: GPS = Global Positioning System. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following animals is associated with China?
explanation_steps: The giant panda lives only in the mountains of central China and is China's national symbol.
Answer: C.
tips: National animals: panda – China; kangaroo – Australia; camel – Eritrea (emblem).

similar_questions.stem: The giant panda feeds mainly on
explanation_steps: About 99% of its diet is bamboo. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Abraham’s salary is 1000 Nakfa more than twice the salary of Kibrom. If the sum of their salaries is 4000 Nakfa, Abraham’s and Kibrom’s salary, in Nakfa, are respectively
explanation_steps: Let Kibrom = k. Abraham = 2k + 1000.
tips: Test options: only 3000 and 1000 satisfy both conditions.

similar_questions.stem: Sara has 5 more books than twice Lidia's. Together they have 35. How many does Sara have?
explanation_steps: Lidia = l, Sara = 2l + 5; 3l + 5 = 35 → l = 10, Sara = 25. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Greenland is a territory controlled by
explanation_steps: Greenland, the world's largest island, is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark (home rule 1979, self-government 2009).
Answer: D.
tips: Geographically Greenland belongs to North America, politically to Denmark.

similar_questions.stem: Which is the largest island in the world (not counting Australia)?
explanation_steps: Greenland (about 2.1 million km²). Answer: C.

questions.stem: In which economic system is private ownership of the means of production forbidden?
explanation_steps: In communism the means of production (land, factories, capital) are owned collectively/by the state; private ownership of them is abolished.
Capitalism and liberalism are based on private ownership; feudal lords and slave owners privately owned land and people. Answer: C.
tips: Capitalism – private ownership + market; command/communist economy – state ownership + planning.

similar_questions.stem: An economic system in which prices are set by supply and demand and resources are privately owned is
explanation_steps: That is capitalism (market economy). Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Business and Economics Grade 10 (economic systems)

questions.stem: The first system of writing was invented in
explanation_steps: Cuneiform writing developed in Sumer (southern Mesopotamia, modern Iraq) around 3400–3200 BC – generally considered the earliest writing system.
Egyptian hieroglyphs appeared only slightly later. Answer: A.
tips: Sumer (Mesopotamia) – cuneiform on clay tablets; Egypt – hieroglyphs on papyrus.

similar_questions.stem: The ancient script written with wedge-shaped marks on clay tablets is called
explanation_steps: Cuneiform means ‘wedge-shaped’. Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Egyptian hieroglyphs are nearly as old; most scholars give Mesopotamia priority. Keyed A.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries added a domestically produced aircraft carrier to its naval force, in 2019?
explanation_steps: On 17 December 2019 China commissioned the Shandong, its first aircraft carrier built entirely in China (its first carrier, Liaoning, was a rebuilt Soviet ship).
Answer: A.
tips: Current-affairs military items usually refer to news from the months before the exam.

similar_questions.stem: China's first aircraft carrier, the Liaoning, was rebuilt from a ship bought from
explanation_steps: The Liaoning was the unfinished Soviet carrier Varyag, bought from Ukraine. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Reuters / BBC – ‘China commissions first domestically built aircraft carrier Shandong’, 17 Dec 2019
textbook_ref.note: China has since launched a third carrier, the Fujian (2022).

questions.stem: The African country created by slaves who returned from the USA is
explanation_steps: Liberia was founded from 1822 by the American Colonization Society as a home for freed African-American slaves; it declared independence in 1847.
Its capital Monrovia is named after US President James Monroe. Answer: E.
tips: Liberia (freed American slaves) and Sierra Leone (Freetown – freed British slaves).

similar_questions.stem: The capital of Liberia is named after an American president. It is
explanation_steps: Monrovia – after James Monroe. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is true</u> concerning the work of Louis Pasteur? He discovered
explanation_steps: Louis Pasteur (1822–1895) established the germ theory (microbes cause many diseases), showed that heating kills microbes (pasteurisation), and developed vaccines against anthrax (1881) and rabies (1885).
Answer: E.
tips: Pasteur – germ theory, pasteurisation, rabies and anthrax vaccines; Jenner – smallpox vaccine; Fleming – penicillin.

similar_questions.stem: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
explanation_steps: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin. Answer: B.

questions.stem: If X = 2Y, and 4Y + X + 10 = 70, what is the value of X?
explanation_steps: Substitute X = 2Y: 4Y + 2Y + 10 = 70 → 6Y = 60 → Y = 10.
tips: Trap: 10 is Y, not X.

similar_questions.stem: If A = 3B and A + B = 24, what is A?
explanation_steps: 3B + B = 24 → B = 6, A = 18. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following sicknesses <u>is not</u> caused by microorganisms?
explanation_steps: Meningitis (bacteria/viruses), tuberculosis (bacterium), influenza (virus) and hepatitis (viruses) are infectious diseases.
Hypertension (high blood pressure) is a non-communicable condition linked to diet, stress, age and genes. Answer: E.
tips: Non-communicable: hypertension, diabetes, cancer, heart disease.

similar_questions.stem: Which disease is non-communicable?
explanation_steps: Diabetes is not caused by a pathogen. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization – Noncommunicable diseases fact sheet

questions.stem: How many towns have been destroyed by nuclear bombs in the world, so far?
explanation_steps: Only two nuclear bombs have been used in war: on Hiroshima (6 August 1945) and Nagasaki (9 August 1945), Japan.
Answer: B.
tips: Hiroshima – ‘Little Boy’ (uranium); Nagasaki – ‘Fat Man’ (plutonium).

similar_questions.stem: The first atomic bomb used in war was dropped on
explanation_steps: Hiroshima, 6 August 1945. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

questions.stem: In the alphabetical series of A, AB, ABD, ABDG, what group of alphabets should follow?
explanation_steps: Each group adds one letter: B (A+1), D (B+2), G (D+3). The gaps grow by 1.
Next letter = G + 4 = K → ABDGK. Answer: A.
tips: Convert letters to positions: 1, 2, 4, 7, 11 (differences 1, 2, 3, 4).

similar_questions.stem: What comes next: C, E, H, L, …?

questions.stem: An African country that launched its own satellite in December 2019 is
explanation_steps: Ethiopia's first satellite, ETRSS-1 (Ethiopian Remote Sensing Satellite), was launched from China on 20 December 2019.
Answer: D.
tips: Egypt also launched satellites (e.g. 2019), but ‘its own first satellite in December 2019’ refers to Ethiopia's widely reported ETRSS-1.

similar_questions.stem: Ethiopia's ETRSS-1 satellite (2019) was launched from
explanation_steps: It was launched on a Chinese rocket from Taiyuan, China. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: BBC News – ‘Ethiopia launches its first satellite into space’, 20 Dec 2019

questions.review_flag: Egypt had satellites launched in 2019 (TIBA-1 on 26 Nov, EgyptSat-A on 21 Feb), though not in December; keyed D (Ethiopia, 20 Dec 2019).

questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, what is the length of the hypotenuse if the two shortest sides are 5 cm and 12 cm?
explanation_steps: Pythagoras: c² = a² + b² = 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169.
c = √169 = 13 cm. Answer: C.
tips: Remember Pythagorean triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17.

similar_questions.stem: The two shorter sides of a right triangle are 6 cm and 8 cm. The hypotenuse is

questions.stem: Yonus has no interest ______ sports.
explanation_steps: The noun ‘interest’ takes the preposition ‘in’: interest in something.
Answer: B.
tips: Learn noun + preposition pairs: interest in, reason for, cause of, solution to.

similar_questions.stem: She is good ______ mathematics.
explanation_steps: The adjective ‘good’ takes ‘at’: good at something. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following animals is <u>different</u> from the others?
explanation_steps: Crocodile, lizard, snake and chameleon are reptiles (dry scaly skin, shelled eggs laid on land).
The frog is an amphibian (moist skin, eggs in water, tadpole larva). Answer: B.
tips: Amphibians: frogs, toads, salamanders. Reptiles: snakes, lizards, crocodiles, tortoises.

similar_questions.stem: Which animal is different from the others?
explanation_steps: The bat is a mammal; the others are birds. Answer: C.

questions.stem: In which year was Asmara officially registered as a UNESCO World Heritage?
explanation_steps: ‘Asmara: A Modernist African City’ was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List on 8 July 2017 (Kraków session).
It is Eritrea's first World Heritage Site. Answer: B.
tips: Asmara – UNESCO World Heritage, July 2017.

similar_questions.stem: Asmara was inscribed on the World Heritage List mainly for its
explanation_steps: Its Italian-era modernist (Art Deco, Futurist) buildings. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: UNESCO World Heritage Centre – ‘Asmara: A Modernist African City’ (inscribed 2017)

questions.stem: Most fish do <u>not</u> sink in water because of the presence of
explanation_steps: Bony fish have a gas-filled swim bladder (air bladder) that controls buoyancy.
Fins are for movement and steering; gills for breathing; air sacs are found in birds. Answer: B.
tips: Sharks lack a swim bladder and rely on an oily liver and swimming.

similar_questions.stem: Fish breathe by means of
explanation_steps: Gills absorb oxygen dissolved in water. Answer: B.

questions.stem: One year before Eritrea was liberated, Mengistu Hailemariam, the then president of Ethiopia said, “The capture of ______ means the loss of the Second Ethiopian Army and in turn the loss of Eritrea”.
explanation_steps: One year before liberation (May 1991) is 1990. In February 1990 the EPLF captured the port of Massawa (Operation Fenkil).
Massawa was the supply line of the Second Revolutionary Army in Asmara; its fall cut the army off from the sea, as Mengistu warned. Answer: E.
tips: Use the date clue: 1988 – Afabet; 1990 – Massawa (Fenkil); 1991 – Asmara liberated.

similar_questions.stem: Operation Fenkil, which liberated Massawa, took place in
explanation_steps: February 1990. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – Operation Fenkil (February 1990); Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Eritrea (war of independence)

questions.review_flag: Exact wording of Mengistu's quotation not verified in an accessible source; keyed E from the date clue (Massawa, Feb 1990).

questions.stem: If a person lacks Vitamin K, what health problems will he/she face?

options.C: Blood will not clot if injured

explanation_steps: Vitamin K is needed to make clotting factors (e.g. prothrombin) in the liver; deficiency causes easy bleeding.
Weak bones – vitamin D; night blindness – vitamin A. Answer: C.
tips: K – ‘Koagulation’ (German for clotting).

similar_questions.stem: Night blindness is caused by lack of vitamin
explanation_steps: Vitamin A is needed for the light-sensitive pigment in the retina. Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements – Vitamin K fact sheet

questions.stem: The biological death of a patient means death of tissues of the
explanation_steps: Clinical death = heartbeat and breathing stop; biological death follows a few minutes later when brain cells, the most sensitive to lack of oxygen, die irreversibly.
Answer: B.
tips: First aid: brain damage begins after about 4–6 minutes without oxygen – start CPR quickly.

similar_questions.stem: Brain cells begin to die after about how many minutes without oxygen?
explanation_steps: About 4–6 minutes. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: First-aid manuals (Red Cross) – clinical vs biological death

questions.stem: Clear nights are colder than cloudy nights because of
explanation_steps: At night the ground loses heat by (infrared) radiation. Clouds absorb and re-radiate this heat back down; on clear nights it escapes to space, so it gets colder.
Answer: C.
tips: Clear skies → strong radiation cooling → frost in the highlands.

similar_questions.stem: Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth through space by
explanation_steps: Only radiation can cross a vacuum. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Radiation fog / terrestrial radiation

questions.stem: Which of the following countries <u>is different</u> from the others?
explanation_steps: Libya, Yemen, Syria and Oman are Arab countries (Arabic-speaking, Arab League members).
Afghanistan is not Arab (its languages are Pashto and Dari). Answer: B.
tips: Many Muslim countries are not Arab: Afghanistan, Iran, Turkey, Pakistan.

similar_questions.stem: Which country is NOT a member of the Arab League?
explanation_steps: Iran (Persian-speaking) is not a member. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: League of Arab States – member states

questions.stem: Watt is an electrical unit of
explanation_steps: The watt (W) is the SI unit of power: 1 W = 1 joule per second = 1 volt × 1 ampere.
Current – ampere; charge – coulomb; potential difference – volt. Answer: D.
tips: P = V × I (watts = volts × amperes).

similar_questions.stem: The unit of electric current is the
explanation_steps: Ampere (A). Answer: B.

questions.stem: The USA bought the state of Alaska from
explanation_steps: In 1867 the USA bought Alaska from the Russian Empire for 7.2 million dollars.
Answer: A.
tips: The USA also bought Louisiana from France (1803).

similar_questions.stem: From which country did the USA buy the Louisiana territory in 1803?
explanation_steps: The Louisiana Purchase was from Napoleon's France. Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the following resources <u>is not</u> renewable.
explanation_steps: Fish, trees and crops can regrow, and sunlight is inexhaustible – renewable.
Copper is a mineral formed over geological time; once mined it cannot be replaced. Answer: E.
tips: Minerals and fossil fuels are non-renewable.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-renewable resource?
explanation_steps: Gold is a mineral – non-renewable. Answer: C.

questions.stem: A container contains 40 liters of milk. From this container, 4 liters of milk was taken out and replaced by water. This process was repeated twice. How many liters does the container have?
explanation_steps: Each time 4 L is removed and 4 L of water is added back, so the total volume in the container stays 40 L.
(The amount of pure milk left after two such operations is 40 × 0.9 × 0.9 = 32.4 L, which is not an option.) Answer: E.
tips: Read exactly what is asked: total liquid, not milk.

similar_questions.stem: A 20 L can of juice: 2 L are removed and replaced by water, twice. How much pure juice remains?

questions.review_flag: Ambiguous: if the question means pure milk, the answer is 32.4 L (not offered); keyed E (total volume 40 L).

questions.stem: How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in a day?
explanation_steps: The minute hand gains 330° per hour on the hour hand, so they coincide every 12/11 hours ≈ 1 h 5 min 27 s.
In 12 hours they coincide 11 times (not 12, because the 11–12 o'clock meeting is at 12:00); in 24 hours 22 times. Answer: C.
tips: Coincide 22 times, opposite 22 times, at right angles 44 times per day.

similar_questions.stem: How many times are the hands of a clock at right angles in 12 hours?
explanation_steps: Twice per coincidence cycle: 2 × 11 = 22 in 12 hours (44 per day). Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a scientific name of lie detector which is used by police for proving lies?
explanation_steps: A polygraph records several body responses at once (pulse, blood pressure, breathing, sweating) while a person answers questions – used as a ‘lie detector’.
Calligraphy is decorative handwriting; a seismometer records earthquakes; a cardiograph records heartbeats only. Answer: B.
tips: poly = many, graph = record: many body signals recorded.

similar_questions.stem: An electrocardiograph (ECG) records the activity of the
explanation_steps: cardio = heart. Answer: B.

questions.stem: One of the following gases is being developed as fuel.
explanation_steps: Hydrogen burns (or reacts in fuel cells) to give energy and only water: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. It is being developed as a clean fuel for vehicles and industry.
Oxygen supports burning but is not a fuel; N₂, CO₂ and O₃ are not fuels. Answer: D.
tips: Fuel = substance that releases energy when it burns/reacts; oxygen is the oxidiser.

similar_questions.stem: The only product formed when hydrogen burns in air is
explanation_steps: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: US Department of Energy – Hydrogen and fuel cells

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs are chemically most <u>dissimilar</u>?
explanation_steps: Sugar and paper are both carbohydrates (sucrose, cellulose); charcoal and diamond are both carbon; chalk and marble are both calcium carbonate.

Butter is a fat (esters of glycerol and fatty acids, containing oxygen) while paraffin wax is a mixture of hydrocarbons (only C and H) – chemically quite different although they look alike. Answer: B.
tips: Look past appearance: similar-looking substances can be chemically different, and different-looking ones chemically alike.

similar_questions.stem: Which pair are made of the same chemical substance?
explanation_steps: Both are calcium carbonate, CaCO₃. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Paraffin wax; Fat; Calcium carbonate

questions.stem: Given 3, 5, 7, 12, 17, 19, which number is different from the others?
explanation_steps: 3, 5, 7, 17 and 19 are prime numbers (and odd).
12 is composite and even. Answer: D.
tips: Check primes/composites and odd/even first in number odd-one-out items.

similar_questions.stem: Which number is different: 2, 11, 13, 21, 23?
explanation_steps: 21 = 3 × 7 is composite; the others are prime. Answer: D.

questions.stem: If in a particular language, A = 0, B = 1, C = 2,..., Y = 25, Z = 26 then what is the value of 2020 (in the form of alphabets only)?
explanation_steps: Using A = 0, B = 1, C = 2: the digits 2, 0, 2, 0 become C, A, C, A → CACA. Answer: E.
Note: the code as printed is inconsistent (with A = 0 we should have Y = 24 and Z = 25), but only CACA fits the stated values of A, B and C.
tips: Code the number digit by digit using the given key.

similar_questions.stem: If A = 1, B = 2, …, Z = 26, what is the sum of the letters in CAB?
explanation_steps: C + A + B = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6. Answer: B.

questions.review_flag: Printed code is inconsistent (A = 0 but Y = 25, Z = 26). Keyed E (CACA) from A = 0, B = 1, C = 2.

questions.stem: Which of the following was named ‘tournament's most valuable player’ during the 15th CECAFA Senior Challenge Cup of 2019?
explanation_steps: Eritrea's captain Robel Teklemichael was voted the best player (MVP) of the 2019 CECAFA Senior Challenge Cup in Uganda, where Eritrea reached the final.
Answer: A.
tips: Eritrean sports achievements are popular GK items – follow ENFF and Eri-TV sports news.

similar_questions.stem: In the 2019 CECAFA Senior Challenge Cup final, Eritrea lost to
explanation_steps: Uganda won 3–0 in Kampala. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean National Football Federation – ‘Impressive Tekle voted 2019 CECAFA Senior Challenge Cup Best Player’

questions.stem: The headquarters of the International Court of Justice is located at
explanation_steps: The ICJ, the main judicial organ of the UN, sits in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.
The Eritrea–Yemen and Eritrea–Ethiopia arbitrations were also held in The Hague (Permanent Court of Arbitration). Answer: A.
tips: UN seats: New York (HQ), Geneva, Vienna, Nairobi; ICJ – The Hague.

similar_questions.stem: The International Criminal Court (ICC) is also based in
explanation_steps: The ICC sits in The Hague. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: International Court of Justice – The Court (icj-cij.org)

questions.stem: What number should come next in the series 173, 196, 219, 242?
explanation_steps: Next: 242 + 23 = 265. Answer: A.
tips: Constant difference → arithmetic sequence.

similar_questions.stem: What comes next: 108, 125, 142, 159, …?
explanation_steps: Common difference 17: 159 + 17 = 176. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following islands is <u>different</u> from the others?
explanation_steps: Madagascar, Seychelles, Iceland and Japan are islands (or island groups) that are countries.
Australia is so large that it is classed as a continent (the ‘island continent’), not an island. Answer: B.
tips: Greenland is the largest island; Australia is counted as a continent.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is an island country in the Indian Ocean?
explanation_steps: Mauritius lies in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Selam has blue blood. According to this statement, Selam

options.C: is of a noble birth or descent.

explanation_steps: ‘Blue blood’ is an idiom for noble or aristocratic birth.
(‘Feeling blue’ would mean sad – a trap for B.) Answer: C.
tips: Colour idioms: blue blood – noble; feeling blue – sad; green with envy – jealous; red-handed – caught in the act.

similar_questions.stem: ‘He was caught red-handed’ means he was

options.B: caught in the act of doing wrong

explanation_steps: Caught while committing the offence. Answer: B.

questions.stem: What is the average of the first five multiples of 12?
explanation_steps: The first five multiples: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60. Sum = 180.
Average = 180 ÷ 5 = 36 (the middle term of an arithmetic sequence). Answer: A.
tips: Average of evenly spaced numbers = middle number.

similar_questions.stem: What is the average of the first four multiples of 5?

questions.stem: The highlands of Eritrea are much cooler than the lowlands. This is due to

options.D: the fact that they are farther from the sun than the lowlands.

explanation_steps: Temperature falls by about 6.5 °C for every 1000 m of height (lapse rate). Asmara (about 2,350 m) is therefore much cooler than Massawa or Tesseney at the same latitude.
Being higher does not bring you meaningfully closer to or farther from the Sun. Answer: C.
tips: Altitude, not latitude, explains Eritrea's cool highlands.

similar_questions.stem: If the temperature at sea level is 30 °C, about what is it at 2000 m (lapse rate 6.5 °C per 1000 m)?

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Geography textbooks (climate of Eritrea); WMO – environmental lapse rate

questions.stem: Which of the following ethnic group in Eritrea speaks a language which belongs to the Nilotic group?
explanation_steps: Nara (and Kunama) speak Nilo-Saharan languages, commonly described in Eritrean sources as Nilotic.
Bilen, Afar and Hidareb (Beja) are Cushitic; Tigre is Semitic. Answer: D.
tips: Nilotic/Nilo-Saharan: Kunama, Nara – both in Gash-Barka.

similar_questions.stem: The Hidareb ethnic group speaks a language of which family?
explanation_steps: Hidareb speak Tu-Bedawie (Beja), a Cushitic language. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – Eritrea's nine ethnic groups; Ethnologue – Nara (Nilo-Saharan, Eastern Sudanic)

questions.stem: A football team won 10 games from the total they played. This was 40 % of the total. How many games were played all in all?
explanation_steps: Check: 40% of 25 = 10. Answer: C.
tips: Whole = part ÷ percentage.

similar_questions.stem: A student answered 18 questions correctly, which was 60% of the test. How many questions were on the test?

questions.stem: The layer of the atmosphere that has great influence on our daily life and activities is the
explanation_steps: The troposphere, the lowest layer (up to about 8–16 km), contains about 75% of the air mass and almost all water vapour; all weather occurs there and we live in it.
Answer: B.
tips: Layers from the ground up: troposphere, stratosphere (ozone), mesosphere, thermosphere, exosphere.

similar_questions.stem: The ozone layer is found mainly in the
explanation_steps: The ozone layer is in the stratosphere. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: NOAA / NASA – Layers of the atmosphere

questions.stem: How many bytes are equal to one kilobyte?
explanation_steps: In computing, 1 kilobyte = 2¹⁰ = 1024 bytes.
(The SI definition, 1 kB = 1000 bytes, is used by some manufacturers; the IEC name for 1024 bytes is kibibyte.) Answer: D.
tips: Powers of 2: 2¹⁰ = 1024.

similar_questions.stem: How many kilobytes are there in one megabyte (binary)?
explanation_steps: 1 MB = 1024 KB. Answer: C.

questions.review_flag: B (1000) is the SI/decimal kilobyte; keyed D (1024), the traditional computing value.

questions.stem: Which of the following words will come in the middle if all are arranged alphabetically as in a dictionary?
explanation_steps: Alphabetical order: Bicycle (bic), Bifocal (bif), Bishop (bis), Bitter (bit), Brink (br).
The third (middle) word is Bishop. Answer: A.
tips: Compare letter by letter until the words differ.

similar_questions.stem: Which word comes first in a dictionary?
explanation_steps: ‘Plan’ is a prefix of the others, so it comes first. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries was <u>not</u> colonized by Italy?
explanation_steps: Italy's colonies were Eritrea (1890), Italian Somaliland and Libya (1911–12).
Djibouti was French Somaliland (French Territory of the Afars and Issas) until 1977. Ethiopia was invaded and occupied by Italy (1936–1941) but is usually described as never colonized. Answer: C.
tips: French in the Horn: Djibouti; British: British Somaliland, Sudan; Italian: Eritrea, Italian Somaliland.

similar_questions.stem: Which European country colonized Djibouti?
explanation_steps: France (French Somaliland) until independence in 1977. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: Encyclopaedia Britannica (britannica.com) – Djibouti (history); Italian colonial empire

questions.review_flag: Ethiopia (E) was occupied by Italy 1936–41 but is usually considered never colonized; keyed C (Djibouti – French colony).

questions.stem: The yellow colour in the Eritrean flag represents

options.A: the priceless blood that was paid by Eritrea's children for independence.
options.B: Eritrea's wealth coming from farming and pastoralism.
options.E: the 30 years of Eritrea’s armed struggle.

explanation_steps: In the Eritrean flag: green = agriculture and livestock; blue = the sea (marine resources); red = the blood shed for independence; the yellow (gold) olive wreath = mineral wealth.
Answer: D. (The 30 leaves of the olive wreath stand for the 30 years of struggle.)
tips: Flag: green – farming; blue – sea; red – blood of martyrs; yellow – minerals; olive branch with 30 leaves – 30 years of struggle, peace.

similar_questions.stem: In the Eritrean flag, the blue colour represents
explanation_steps: Blue stands for the Red Sea and its resources. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – National flag of Eritrea (meaning of colours)

questions.stem: The energy efficient stove for making injera is known by the name
explanation_steps: The improved injera stove ‘Adhanet’ (Tigrinya for ‘saviour’), developed by the Energy Research and Training Centre, uses about half the firewood of a traditional open mogogo.
Answer: B.
tips: Adhanet saves wood, reduces smoke and protects women's health and the forest.

similar_questions.stem: The main environmental benefit of the Adhanet stove is
explanation_steps: It uses much less biomass fuel. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrea Ministry of Information (shabait.com) – Adhanet improved mogogo stove; Ashden Awards – Eritrea improved injera stove

questions.stem: The scientist who first argued that the sun is at the center of the Solar System, and that the Earth and other planets revolve around the sun was
explanation_steps: Nicolaus Copernicus set out the heliocentric (Sun-centred) model in ‘On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres’ (1543).
Galileo later supported it with telescope observations and Kepler described the planets' elliptical orbits. Answer: A.
tips: Ancient Greek Aristarchus had the idea earlier, but Copernicus is credited with the scientific heliocentric model.

similar_questions.stem: Who discovered that the planets move in elliptical orbits?
explanation_steps: Johannes Kepler's first law (1609). Answer: B.

questions.stem: From the following choose the odd one.
explanation_steps: Protestantism, Catholicism, Buddhism and Judaism are religions (or branches of religions).
Socialism is a political and economic ideology. Answer: E.
tips: Identify the common category first (religions).

similar_questions.stem: Which one is different?
explanation_steps: Islam is a religion; the others are forms of government. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following players was nominated Africa’s player of the year in 2019?
explanation_steps: The 2019 CAF African Player of the Year, announced in Hurghada on 7 January 2020, was Sadio Mané (Senegal, Liverpool); Mohamed Salah and Riyad Mahrez were the other finalists.
The item clearly means ‘named’ Player of the Year. Answer: D.
tips: CAF Player of the Year: 2017 Salah, 2018 Salah, 2019 Mané.

similar_questions.stem: Which Egyptian player won the CAF African Player of the Year award in both 2017 and 2018?
explanation_steps: Mohamed Salah (Liverpool) won in 2017 and 2018. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: CAF Awards 2019 (7 January 2020) – African Player of the Year: Sadio Mané

questions.review_flag: Wording ‘nominated’: Salah (A) was also a finalist/nominee in 2019. Keyed D as the winner (Mané).

questions.stem: What was the justification that the USA used to invade Iraq in 2003?

options.B: Iraq increased the price of oil.
options.C: Iraq refused to sell oil to the USA.
options.D: Iraq was planning to attack the USA.
options.E: Iraq had weapons of mass destruction.

explanation_steps: The US and UK justified the March 2003 invasion by claiming Saddam Hussein's Iraq possessed weapons of mass destruction (none were found).
The invasion of Kuwait (1990) led to the 1991 Gulf War, not the 2003 war. Answer: E.
tips: 1991 Gulf War – liberation of Kuwait; 2003 Iraq War – alleged WMD.

similar_questions.stem: The 1991 Gulf War was fought to

options.D: stop a civil war in Syria

explanation_steps: The coalition expelled Iraqi forces from Kuwait. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The tallest mountain in the world is Mount
explanation_steps: Mount Everest in the Himalayas (Nepal–China) is the highest mountain above sea level, 8,849 m.
Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) is Africa's highest; Aconcagua South America's; Elbrus Europe's. Answer: E.
tips: Highest peak per continent: Everest (Asia), Aconcagua (S. America), Denali (N. America), Kilimanjaro (Africa), Elbrus (Europe).

similar_questions.stem: The highest mountain in Eritrea is
explanation_steps: Emba Soira (about 3,018 m) near Senafe. Answer: A.

questions.stem: If income remains unchanged, but price of goods increases, what will happen to workers?

options.B: Their ability to buy goods will decrease.
options.D: Their consumption of good will decrease.

explanation_steps: With the same money income and higher prices, the real income (purchasing power) falls.
So workers can buy less, consume less and usually save less. Answer: E.
tips: Real income = money income ÷ price level.

similar_questions.stem: If a worker's salary rises by 10% while prices rise by 15%, her real income
explanation_steps: Prices rise faster than income, so real income falls (by about 4–5%). Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: Eritrean MoE Business and Economics Grade 12 (inflation and real income)

questions.stem: The 2020 FIFA World Cup will be hosted by
explanation_steps: There is no 2020 World Cup: the next World Cup after Russia 2018 was the 2022 FIFA World Cup, hosted by Qatar (November–December 2022).
The intended answer is Qatar. Answer: B.
tips: World Cups are every four years: 2014 Brazil, 2018 Russia, 2022 Qatar, 2026 USA/Canada/Mexico.

similar_questions.stem: Which country won the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar?
explanation_steps: Argentina beat France on penalties. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.note: The 2022 tournament has since taken place (Argentina won); the 2026 World Cup is in the USA, Canada and Mexico.

questions.review_flag: Printed error: there was no ‘2020’ World Cup – the paper means the 2022 World Cup (Qatar).

questions.stem: Besides carbohydrates, the major source of energy in our food is/are
explanation_steps: Fats give about 9 kcal (37 kJ) per gram – more than twice carbohydrates or proteins (about 4 kcal/g) – and are the body's main energy store.
Vitamins, minerals and water give no energy. Answer: B.
tips: Energy foods: carbohydrates and fats; body-building: proteins; protective: vitamins and minerals.

similar_questions.stem: Which nutrient gives the most energy per gram?
explanation_steps: Fat: about 9 kcal/g. Answer: C.

textbook_ref.reference: FAO – Food energy: methods of analysis and conversion factors

questions.stem: Which of the following food constituents <u>is not</u> digested but is still important for us?
explanation_steps: Dietary fibre (roughage, mainly cellulose) cannot be digested by human enzymes, but it adds bulk, helps movement of food through the gut and prevents constipation.
Answer: D.
tips: Fibre sources: vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes.

similar_questions.stem: Lack of fibre in the diet mainly causes
explanation_steps: Fibre helps bowel movement; without it constipation occurs. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: WHO – Healthy diet; Harvard T.H. Chan School – Fiber

questions.review_flag: Vitamins and minerals are also absorbed without being ‘digested’ (broken down), but fibre is the standard answer. Keyed D.

questions.stem: The capital city of Rwanda is
explanation_steps: Kigali is the capital of Rwanda.
Kampala – Uganda; Nairobi – Kenya; Lusaka – Zambia; Bujumbura – former capital of Burundi. Answer: B.
tips: Burundi moved its capital from Bujumbura to Gitega (2019).

similar_questions.stem: What is the capital of Burundi today?
explanation_steps: Gitega became the political capital in 2019. Answer: B.

questions.stem: I think, I understood the ______ and bolts of the operation.
explanation_steps: The idiom ‘the nuts and bolts’ means the basic practical details of how something works.
Answer: B.
tips: Fixed pairs: nuts and bolts, bread and butter, pros and cons.

similar_questions.stem: ‘The pros and cons of a plan’ are its
explanation_steps: Pros = for, cons = against. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Plants look green because they
explanation_steps: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly red and blue light for photosynthesis and reflects (and transmits) green light, which reaches our eyes.
Answer: D.
tips: An object's colour = the colour of light it reflects.

similar_questions.stem: A red shirt looks red because it
explanation_steps: It reflects red and absorbs the other colours. Answer: B.

questions.stem: How do you distinguish a planet from a star with your naked eye?

options.A: Every planet shines brighter than every star.
options.B: Stars twinkle, but planets do not.
options.C: Planets twinkle, but stars do not.
options.D: Planets can be seen with a telescope, but stars cannot.
options.E: Planets have long tails, but stars do not have tails.

explanation_steps: Stars are so far away that they look like points; the atmosphere makes their light flicker (twinkle). Planets show tiny discs, so their light is steadier.
Not every planet is brighter than every star; comets, not planets, have tails. Answer: B.
tips: Rule of thumb: twinkling point – star; steady light – planet.

similar_questions.stem: The brightest planet in the night sky, often called the morning or evening star, is
explanation_steps: Venus. Answer: B.

questions.stem: If January 1, 1996, was Monday, what day of the week was January 1, 1997?
explanation_steps: 1996 is a leap year (divisible by 4): 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 days.
Monday + 2 days = Wednesday. Answer: B.
tips: Ordinary year: +1 weekday; leap year: +2 weekdays.

similar_questions.stem: If 1 January 2023 was a Sunday, what day was 1 January 2024?
explanation_steps: 2023 is not a leap year: 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 day → Monday. Answer: B.

questions.stem: How many days are there in x weeks and x days?
explanation_steps: x weeks = 7x days; plus x days → 7x + x = 8x days.
Answer: B.
tips: Convert everything to the same unit before adding.

similar_questions.stem: How many hours are there in y days and y hours?
explanation_steps: 24y + y = 25y hours. Answer: A.

questions.review_flag: Options printed as ‘7x2’ and ‘x2’ are read as 7x² and x².

questions.stem: Which of the following <u>is not</u> an input device of a computer?
explanation_steps: Keyboard, mouse, joystick and microphone send data into the computer (input).
The monitor displays information from the computer (output). Answer: E.
tips: Input → processing (CPU) → output.

similar_questions.stem: Which device is used for both input and output?
explanation_steps: A touchscreen displays output and accepts touch input. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following authors wrote a book about Hamid Idris Awate?
explanation_steps: The biography ‘Hamid Idris Awate 1915–1962’ (2018, Hdri Publishers) was written by veteran journalist and fighter Haileselasie Weldu after about 35 years of research.
Answer: A.
tips: Recent Eritrean books launched in Asmara are reported on shabait.com – a common source for GK items.

similar_questions.stem: Hamid Idris Awate is remembered for

options.B: firing the first shot of the armed struggle in 1961

explanation_steps: He began the armed struggle at Mount Adal on 1 September 1961. Answer: B.

questions.stem: We can take care of our environment by doing all of the following, <u>except</u>
explanation_steps: Planting trees, keeping surroundings clean, terracing/dams and saving water protect the environment.
Heavy use of firewood causes deforestation and smoke. Answer: D.
tips: Eritrean environmental campaigns: afforestation, terracing, Adhanet stoves, Green Campaign.

similar_questions.stem: Which activity helps to reduce soil erosion on hillsides?
explanation_steps: Terraces slow runoff. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following cities is found in Zoba Anseba?
explanation_steps: Hamelmalo (seat of Hamelmalo Agricultural College) is a sub-zone of Zoba Anseba near Keren.
Sheeb is in the Northern Red Sea; Mogolo, Tokombiya and Logo Anseba are sub-zones of Gash-Barka (Logo Anseba is named after the Anseba river, but it is not in Zoba Anseba). Answer: D.
tips: Beware of names: ‘Logo Anseba’ is in Gash-Barka.

similar_questions.stem: The capital of Zoba Anseba is
explanation_steps: Keren. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following substances interacts with calcium to build strong bones?
explanation_steps: Bone mineral is calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite): phosphorus combines with calcium to form the hard part of bones and teeth.
Vitamin D helps the intestine absorb calcium and is also essential for strong bones, so A is defensible too. Answer: C (A also accepted).
tips: Bone needs calcium + phosphorus (the mineral) and vitamin D (for absorption).

similar_questions.stem: The hard mineral of bones and teeth is mainly
explanation_steps: Calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite). Answer: A.

textbook_ref.reference: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements – Calcium; Phosphorus; Vitamin D fact sheets

questions.review_flag: Two defensible options: phosphorus (C) combines with calcium in bone; vitamin D (A) enables calcium absorption. Both accepted.

questions.stem: A diet high in saturated fats can be linked to
explanation_steps: Saturated fats raise LDL (‘bad’) cholesterol, which leads to fatty deposits in arteries (atherosclerosis), heart attacks and strokes – cardiovascular diseases.
Bulimia and anorexia are eating disorders. Answer: C.
tips: Saturated fats: butter, fatty meat, ghee; unsaturated: vegetable oils, fish.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following is high in unsaturated (healthier) fat?
explanation_steps: Olive oil is rich in unsaturated fat. Answer: B.

textbook_ref.reference: World Health Organization – Cardiovascular diseases; Healthy diet
